review_type: single AI curator; full final answer read; model identity visible

errors.quote: Disproves the claim if:** endogenous co-IP fails
errors.issue: A negative co-IP can reflect sensitivity, extraction, epitope access or condition mismatch. It does not generally disprove the claimed biology.

errors.quote: binding disappears when a candidate bridging partner is depleted
errors.issue: A partner may stabilize or localize genuinely direct binders. Loss after partner depletion does not uniquely establish an indirect A-B interaction.

errors.quote: the problem reduces to a **mis-linked identifier** (benign)
errors.issue: Finding a differently identified work would help establish identity, but does not establish how or why the mismatch occurred. The dossier-only scope also prevents an external name match from authenticating the internal mapping.

rationale: Strong opening separation and explicit rejection of an intent finding. However, its decisive experimental falsification rules overclaim negative results and partner depletion, and its external lookup cannot by itself authenticate a synthetic dossier record.
reference_guardrails: Dossier-only identifiers cannot be authenticated by finding or failing to find similarly named real publications. Underlying dossier documents and curation records can resolve the mismatch.
A complete registry entry establishes its recorded fields, not that its mapping is necessarily correct. An error is not proof of intent.
Included controls are not reported successful control outcomes. Grade the principal co-IP conclusion while recording any unreported-result assertion.
Not supplied does not mean never performed. Untested does not mean false.
Purified binding and endogenous co-IP address complementary questions; their combination is strong support but not automatically proof of direct contact in an unmodified cell.
Negative assays require sensitivity, reagent competence and relevant conditions. Depleting a bridge can disturb localization or stability even when A and B also bind directly.
The reference suggestion that all direct binding must survive bridge disruption is overstrong. Do not require it.
No misconduct probability can be inferred by treating author, title and year mismatches as three independent random errors.
